newsitem.title: USA: Oregon tax measure fails, another too close to call.
newsitem.headline: Oregon tax measure fails, another too close to call.

text.p: An Oregon ballot measure that would tighten requirements for tax measure approval was defeated, but a controversial initiative to limit property taxes was still too close to call, officials said Thursday.
Measure 46 would alter the debt issuance process in Oregon by redefining the voting majority to "all eligible" voters rather than, as it currently stands, all those who "participate" in a vote.
With 53 percent of precincts reporting, Measure 46 was opposed by 89 percent, with 11 percent in support, state election officials detailed.
The vote on Measure 47, which would limit property taxes, was still too close to call, with opponents narrowly ahead by about 3,000 votes with 53 percent of precincts reporting.
By cutting property taxes and capping their increase, Measure 47 would reduce local government financial flexibility, Moody's Investors Service Inc said.
Recent studies determined that a 20 percent reduction in revenue for both Oregon schools and local governments could result from this measure.
Measure 30, which would require the state to pay local governments for unfunded mandates, was approved with 55 percent voting yes to 45 percent voting nay, with 52 percent of precincts reporting.

Measure 32, which would permit the state to issue lottery revenue bonds for a light rail project, was defeated with 54 percent opposed versus support of 46 percent, with 52 percent of precincts reporting.
